_note: Retired URLs -> where they now point. build-redirects.js writes a redirect stub (canonical + meta refresh + JS) at each old path. NOTE 2026-09-23: this note used to say the stubs were noindex. They are not, and must not be — noindex plus a canonical is a contradictory instruction and would tell Google to drop the URL rather than pass its signals to the target. The stubs are deliberately indexable so the meta refresh reads as a permanent redirect and the old URL's equity consolidates into the new one. Impressions still logged against a stub in Search Console are the lagging record of a redirect Google has already followed, not evidence that the ranking is being thrown away. GitHub Pages has no server-side 301s; Google treats an instant meta refresh as a permanent redirect. Rules expand at build time: '*' in a key matches a single path segment and is substituted into the target. Heavy haul was retired as a service line in the 2026-09 revamp. 2026-09-21: two trailer URLs were un-retired and rebuilt as dispatch-framed guides because they still rank (1,729 and 543 impressions) and the people searching them are fleet owners choosing trailers, which is the 4+ truck dispatch buyer. The heavy-haul, oversize-permit, pilot-car and superload stubs stay stubbed on purpose: that demand wants a motor carrier. 2026-09-23: the five remaining trailer-name stubs (552 impressions between them) were repointed off the generic pillars and onto the matching dispatch desk built on 2026-09-22 — step deck, RGN/lowboy and Conestoga now have exact-match targets, so sending trailer-shoppers to /services/project-freight was throwing away the match. Same reasoning as the 09-21 note, now that the pages exist. Comparison queries (flatbed-vs-step-deck, rgn-vs-lowboy, drop-deck-vs-flatbed, step-deck-dimensions) stay on /trailer-selector: that is comparison intent, not one-trailer intent. /services/flatbed-transport stays on /services/dedicated-lanes because 'flatbed transport' is someone buying transport, not a fleet owner shopping trailers.
